endorsements.quote: Implementation can also be staged: start with one high‐burden workflow, co‐define the decision view with frontline nurses, configure the view (or use structured templates where configuration is limited), and audit a small indicator set—alert overrides, documentation time, navigation burden, and omission‐prone near‐miss patterns—before scaling.

Alert override rate Increased proportion of alerts overridden or dismissed, including critical categories EHR log data A behavioural marker of alarm fatigue and loss of trust in the signal stream (Deb and Claudio 2015 )
Every displayed signal must specify: recommended next step, owner, timeframe, and link to the relevant workflow (order set/referral/escalation route); retire non‐actionable items

Governance also matters for automation. When models are updated, when data drift occurs, or when generative tools are introduced, Trust gate requirements (rationale, provenance, recency, missingness information, uncertainty) should be treated as minimum deployment criteria and re‐checked after updates (Awad et al. 2025 ; Tong et al. 2025 ).

Implementation can also be staged: start with one high‐burden workflow, co‐define the decision view with frontline nurses, configure the view (or use structured templates where configuration is limited), and audit a small indicator set—alert overrides, documentation time, navigation burden, and omission‐prone near‐miss patterns—before scaling.
The framework only helps if it reduces work rather than shifting it elsewhere.

unlisted_practices: Present automated scores and flags with plain-language rationale, provenance, recency, missingness information, and an uncertainty indicator, and do not give them prominence otherwise.
Retire measures, documentation fields, and alerts that are not linked to a decision point or treatment goal.
Apply a 'one in, one out' rule so any new measure, alert, or score must justify its decision value and displace an existing lower-value requirement.
Remove or redesign any gate rule that increases steps or shifts work onto nurses without measurable gain in signal-to-noise or follow-through.
Re-tier alerts by patient acuity and workflow stage and retire low-value alerts using log data.
Build transition-specific views showing what changed, what is pending, and what needs watching next, with person-specific triggers and protective factors visible.
Monitor suppression safety through near-miss patterns, escalation delays, and responsiveness to critical alerts after re-tiering.
Evaluate whether curated decision views improve or worsen equity in cue visibility, escalation, and continuity.
Teach cognitive safety as part of digital competence in nursing education.

screen.reason: Structured debates essay proposing a conceptual framework (Cognitive Firewall / Minimum Viable Data) to govern automated scores and clinical decision support to reduce cognitive overload and burnout in mental health nursing.
